items.title: Manuel Joseph "Moose" Zanco Interview, 1959-11-25
items.q: I was, uh, fortunate enough to catch, uh, Wilbert DiPerry's group in New York.

ctx.x: But he's back on the Cornet, and you even see modern guys now going to the Cornet, like, I heard Melvin last year, uh, I think it was Friday night, uh, at, uh, the jazz room on Dolphin Street, you know? Yeah, at the corner. And, uh, he was playing Cornet.

Well, uh, I was, uh, fortunate enough to catch, uh, Wilbert DiPerry's group in New York. And, uh, Sidney DiPerry has both a trumpet and a Cornet. He hangs them both on his music stand. Now, whichever tune they play, the type of tune he plays, that, you know, that's the decided fact as to which instrument he will use. If they play the real old New Orleans, uh, Mark stuff, he takes his cornet. If he plays something, maybe more of a, uh, a dance tune, he'll use his trumpet.
Hmm. Well, one more thing I wanted to ask you about was that compliment you told me you got.
